paper_title: NASDUCK: New Constraints on Axion-like Dark Matter from Floquet Quantum Detector
suggested_experiment_name: NASDUCK (Noble and Alkali Spin Detectors for Ultralight Coherent darK matter)
notes: Paper reports new constraints on ALP-neutron couplings in the mass range 4×10^-15 to 4×10^-12 eV/c^2. The abstract states the bounds improve upon previous terrestrial limits by up to 3 orders of magnitude for masses above 4×10^-14 eV/c^2, and partially close the unexplored region for couplings in the range 10^-6 to 2×10^-5 GeV^-1. The coupling values in the abstract (10^-6 to 2×10^-5 GeV^-1) are converted to dimensionless g_an using the standard relation: g_an = g_agamma × (m_a c^2 / (ħc)) for the relevant mass range. However, the paper's main exclusion plots (Figs. 2 and 3) show detailed mass-dependent bounds that vary significantly across the search range. The data_points provided represent the approximate flat coupling range stated in the abstract (10^-6 to 2×10^-5 GeV^-1 ≈ 1×10^-5 dimensionless) as a sentinel two-point bound spanning the full mass range, though the actual experimental limits are more complex and mass-dependent as shown in the figures. The local DM density of 0.4 GeV/cm^3 is explicitly stated in Eq. 2 as the standard halo model value. The experiment uses spin-polarized xenon-129 gas with a rubidium Floquet optical magnetometer, searching for coherent interactions with ultralight ALP dark matter as Earth traverses the galactic halo. All constraints are at 95% C.L.
